analysis:
Examined the docs change plus the two Swift diffs. SandboxAddon.swift (head 154-173, 211-225) adds parsing of an optional `disks` array from `darkbloom-sandbox status --json`: Disk struct, supportsWorkDisks flag, and a private disk() parser. The parser uses only typed JSON casts (as? String/Bool/Int/Int64), clamps slot totals with max(0, ...), and drops malformed entries. It does not execute, path-resolve or write anything. The `path` and `detail` strings come from the add-on, which TB-013/T-061 already treat as running with the owner's authority, and they are only displayed. No new trust boundary is crossed.

SandboxEligibility.swift (head 247-263, 312-320) adds an informational `Work disk` check line and a jobCount helper. These are presentation only. A compile-level concern: `diskChecks` uses `disks` and `disk.floorBytes`, which are not in the visible SandboxSizingPlan or Disk definitions. SandboxSizingPlan is defined elsewhere and was not supplied, so I cannot confirm the field exists. That is a build/contract question rather than a security one.

The docs describe `--disk <volume>`, `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` and the `--yes` behaviour. Disk selection, the sudo prompt, the installer `--disk` argument construction and drive validation live in unchanged or unsupplied files, such as the setup command and installer runner. I could not review them, including shell/argument quoting of user-supplied volume paths and the sudo invocation. These affect TB-013/T-061 and A-019 and should be checked in the setup command code if it is part of this PR.

No link to the provider-inference threats (T-041 cache storage) was found, because the sandbox work disks are separate from the KV cache volume. No regression was identified in the supplied lines.
